headline: UK inflation jumped to 3.5% in September, above forecasts, making a Bank of England rate hike on November 5 close to certain. Oil climbed back toward $110 as tanker attacks spread to the Gulf of Oman.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: The dollar held steady overnight near 101.8 on the dollar index, close to its lowest in three weeks. Oil edged back up on new tanker attacks, but US 10-year yields barely moved, so the dollar had little reason to move either.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: for three weeks, US–Iran fighting in the Gulf has pushed oil up, and with it US inflation fears, bets on a December Fed hike, and the dollar. On Tuesday a report of a US–Iran peace framework, which neither side confirmed, pulled oil and the dollar back. What changed: very little in Asia. The dollar index sat near 101.8, a touch above Tuesday's close, and the US 10-year Treasury yield held a little above 5.1%. Oil rose again on reports that tanker attacks have spread to the Gulf of Oman, but not by enough to lift yields. Bets on the Fed are unchanged: a hold on October 28 is the strong favourite and a December hike is close to fully priced. What it means: the dollar is moving with oil and long-term yields, not with US news. The question to keep asking: does oil stay high enough to keep the Fed's December hike on the table?
chapters.fx: What's next: no major US data today; government crude oil stocks at 9:30 AM CT. Thursday brings weekly jobless claims at 7:30 AM CT. The Fed stays in its quiet period until its October 28 decision.
numbers: Dollar index ~101.8 (+0.1% overnight; near a three-week low)
Fed: Oct 28 hold ~84%; Dec hike ~90% (CME FedWatch)

scenarios.base: If oil stays near $110 and the peace report stays unconfirmed, the dollar drifts near its three-week low.
scenarios.bull: If Gulf attacks escalate and oil jumps, yields rise and the dollar recovers.
scenarios.bear: If Washington or Tehran confirms a framework, oil and long yields fall and the dollar slips further.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro was flat overnight near $1.123. Higher oil is a cost for the euro area, and France's budget fight still hangs over it, with the key revenue vote now on October 27 and a Moody's review of France on Friday.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: the euro has been held back by France's budget trouble and by expensive energy, which Europe imports. The European Central Bank is expected to hold on October 29 and lean toward a hike in December, because inflation is at a three-year high. What changed: nothing new from Europe overnight. The euro slipped a hair against a steady dollar as oil climbed back toward $110, a reminder that pricier energy is a bill for the euro area. What it means: the euro is caught between two forces. A likely December ECB hike supports it; France's politics and the oil bill weigh on it. The question: does France's budget fight calm down before the ECB acts?
chapters.fx: What's next: Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel speaks at 2:15 AM CT; the Bundesbank's monthly report at 5:00 AM CT. Thursday: the euro area's consumer confidence reading at 9:00 AM CT. Friday: Moody's review of France. October 27: France's revenue vote.
numbers: France revenue vote moved to Oct 27

scenarios.base: If oil holds and France stays quiet until the vote, the euro hovers near $1.12.
scenarios.bull: If oil eases or ECB speakers firm up December, the euro gains.
scenarios.bear: If Moody's turns more negative on France or oil spikes, the euro slips.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September, above the 3.4% expected and the highest in 11 months, driven by energy costs. That locks in a Bank of England rate hike on November 5. The pound sat near $1.337 before the release.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: the war in the Gulf has pushed up energy bills, and Britain, which imports a lot of gas, has felt it more than most. The Bank of England has held rates since February, but strong jobs data on Tuesday made a November hike almost a sure thing. What changed: UK consumer prices, through the four beats. (1) How much prices rose over the past year. (2) 3.5% in September, up from 3.1% in August and above the 3.4% forecast. (3) That is well over the Bank's 2% target and about half a point above its own summer forecast, so the energy shock is not fading. (4) For the pound: a hot print makes a November hike to 4% close to certain and puts a second hike in December up for debate, which keeps UK rates high and supports the pound. What it means: the November hike is no longer the question; December is. The question: how long does the Bank of England think energy will keep inflation up?
chapters.fx: What's next: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey speaks at 8:00 AM CT, his first word after these figures. Thursday: UK consumer confidence at 6:01 PM CT. October 28: Chancellor John Healey's first budget, which may add help with energy bills. November 5: the rate decision.
numbers: UK CPI 3.5% y/y (3.4% expected; 3.1% in August)

scenarios.base: If Bailey backs the November hike without promising more, the pound holds near $1.34.
scenarios.bull: If Bailey sounds open to a second hike in December, UK yields and the pound rise.
scenarios.bear: If Bailey calls the energy jump temporary, December bets fade and the pound gives back some of its gains.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: The yen eased slightly to near 158.3 per dollar. Japan's exports grew less than expected in September and its trade deficit was wider than forecast. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said she sees no gap with the Bank of Japan's view.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: the yen has been weak because US rates are far above Japan's, and because Japan pays more for imported energy when oil is high. The Bank of Japan is expected to hold on October 30 and is seen raising rates in December. What changed: two things. First, Japan's trade figures. (1) The gap between what Japan sells abroad and what it buys. (2) A September deficit of about ¥540 billion, against about ¥180 billion expected, as exports rose 16.7% instead of about 20%. (3) Exports are still growing, but the oil bill keeps eating into them. (4) For the yen, more money leaving Japan to pay for imports is a mild drag. Second, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said the government and the Bank of Japan see things the same way and that wage-driven inflation is near. That backs the case for a December hike. What it means: the yen gets help from a likely December hike but loses some to the oil bill. The question: does Japan's inflation figure, out Thursday evening CT, keep the December hike on track?
chapters.fx: What's next: Japan's national inflation figures at 6:30 PM CT Thursday; October business surveys at 7:30 PM CT Thursday. October 29–30: the Bank of Japan's meeting.

scenarios.base: If US yields stay steady, the yen holds near 158 until the Bank of Japan meets.
scenarios.bull: If Japan's inflation figure comes in hot or Bank of Japan officials back December, the yen firms.
scenarios.bear: If oil climbs further and US yields rise, the yen weakens toward 159.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The franc eased slightly to near 0.826 per dollar with no Swiss news. Against the euro it stays close to its strongest in three months.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: the franc is a safe place to park money in uncertain times, and with fighting in the Gulf and France's budget trouble, it has been strong against the euro. The Swiss National Bank holds rates at zero and could cut in December because Swiss inflation is very low. What changed: nothing Swiss. The franc moved a touch with the dollar overnight; tanker attacks pushed oil up but did not set off a rush into safe havens. What it means: the franc's strength comes from worry elsewhere, not from Switzerland. The question: does fear in the Gulf or in France rise enough to push it further?
chapters.fx: What's next: the SNB's summary of its September policy discussion at 2:30 AM CT Thursday, a read on how worried it is about the strong franc. The next SNB decision is December 10.

scenarios.base: Without a new scare, the franc stays firm against the euro and moves with the dollar.
scenarios.bull: A Gulf escalation or French bond stress sends money into the franc.
scenarios.bear: If the SNB's summary warns about the franc's strength, it gives back some ground against the euro.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The Aussie held near 70.2 US cents, its highest in three weeks. Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said the inflation outlook is materially worse, partly on high oil, lifting bets on a November hike.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: the RBA has raised rates four times this year to 4.60% as inflation stays sticky, and its officials have recently hinted rates may need to go higher still. That has made the Aussie one of the stronger major currencies. What changed: Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said policy is working to slow the economy but the inflation outlook has got materially worse. Markets raised the chance of a November 3 hike to about 40%, from about 30% at the start of the week, and the Aussie climbed to its highest in three weeks. One cooling sign: China's central bank set its daily yuan guide much weaker than expected, a hint it wants to slow the yuan's rise, which can weigh on the Aussie. What it means: the RBA's tone is the main support for the Aussie right now. The question: does next week's inflation report justify a fifth hike?
chapters.fx: What's next: Australia's October business surveys at 5:00 PM CT Thursday. October 28: Australia's third-quarter inflation report, the deciding number. November 2–3: the RBA's decision.
numbers: RBA Nov 3 hike ~40% (Reuters); fully priced by March

scenarios.base: If the dollar stays soft and the RBA's tone holds, the Aussie stays near 70 cents.
scenarios.bull: If more RBA officials echo Hauser, November hike bets climb and the Aussie extends.
scenarios.bear: If China keeps leaning against its currency or risk mood sours, the Aussie gives back its gains.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The loonie held near 1.406 per US dollar, close to its strongest in four weeks. Markets still see a Bank of Canada rate hike on October 28 as very likely, and oil back near $110 adds support.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: the Bank of Canada was expected to hold until Governor Tiff Macklem warned on October 17 that its inflation forecast will be revised substantially higher because of energy. Markets swung toward an October 28 hike, and the loonie climbed. What changed: nothing new from Canada overnight. The loonie barely moved, and higher oil, Canada's biggest export, was a quiet support. What it means: a hike is mostly in the price already, so the loonie needs more than a hike to rise much further; a surprise hold would hit it. The question: does the Bank of Canada deliver what markets expect?
chapters.fx: What's next: Canadian producer prices at 7:30 AM CT Thursday. October 28: the Bank of Canada's decision, with its new forecasts.
numbers: CFTC: hedge funds strongly against CAD

scenarios.base: If hike bets hold and oil stays high, the loonie stays near its four-week best.
scenarios.bull: If oil climbs further, the loonie extends, and funds betting against it may have to cover.
scenarios.bear: If oil drops on a peace deal or Bank of Canada officials cool hike talk, the loonie slips.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The kiwi eased slightly to near 0.568 ahead of New Zealand's third-quarter inflation report at 4:45 PM CT today. Markets give a Reserve Bank of New Zealand hike on October 28 about an 80% chance; this figure decides it.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: New Zealand's central bank has been debating whether to raise rates again on October 28. Business activity is strong and dairy prices firmed this week, but parts of the economy are soft. What changed: no new data overnight; the kiwi dipped slightly as traders waited for the inflation report. What it means: with a hike about 80% priced, a figure near forecast mostly keeps the kiwi where it is, while a clearly soft one would revive talk of a hold. The question: does inflation cool as much as expected?
chapters.fx: What's next: New Zealand's third-quarter inflation report at 4:45 PM CT today (about 3.8% a year expected, from 4.1%; about 0.8% for the quarter). October 28: the RBNZ's decision.

scenarios.base: If inflation lands near 3.8%, hike bets hold and the kiwi stays near 0.57.
scenarios.bull: If inflation comes in hot, the hike looks settled and the kiwi rises.
scenarios.bear: If inflation comes in well below forecast, hold talk returns and the kiwi falls.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Brent climbed back toward $110 overnight, recovering some of Tuesday's drop. Analysts at LSEG say tanker attacks have spread beyond the Strait of Hormuz into the Gulf of Oman, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a supertanker caught fire after hitting a mine.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: since the US–Iran war began in February, oil has carried a large risk premium, and attacks on Gulf shipping and Saudi sites pushed Brent to a five-month high near $112 on Tuesday before a peace report pulled it back. What changed: buyers returned overnight. Analysts at LSEG said attacks have widened to the Gulf of Oman, which threatens cargoes loaded outside the Gulf and the ship-to-ship transfers that kept oil moving. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a supertanker hit a mine south of Hormuz; that claim has not been independently confirmed. US Energy Department officials said they are working with refiners to raise fuel output amid a diesel shortage. What it means: the supply risk is spreading rather than easing, which keeps the risk premium in place and supports oil exporters' currencies like the Canadian dollar while costing importers like the euro and yen. The question: does diplomacy produce anything real before shipping gets worse?
chapters.fx: What's next: US government crude oil stocks at 9:30 AM CT. Any confirmation from Washington or Tehran of the reported framework would cut the premium quickly.
numbers: At least 18 ships attacked in two weeks (Kpler)

scenarios.base: If attacks continue without a big new hit, Brent holds near $110.
scenarios.bull: If a major loading site or tanker route is hit, Brent tops Tuesday's $112 high.
scenarios.bear: If a US–Iran framework is confirmed, the premium drains and Brent falls toward $105.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold slipped to near $4,115 an ounce, a fourth straight daily loss. High oil keeps rate-hike bets alive around the world, and with US 10-year yields above 5%, holding gold, which pays no interest, costs more.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: gold rallied to records earlier in the year on war and inflation fears, but rising interest rates have weighed on it since. What changed: a small further dip overnight, with gold in the lower part of its recent range. Oil's rebound kept expectations of more rate hikes in place, from the Fed in December to the Bank of England in November. What it means: higher rates are beating fear right now. Gold needs either falling yields or a real shock to turn up. The question: do yields keep climbing?
chapters.fx: What's next: US data is light until Thursday's jobless claims at 7:30 AM CT. Gulf headlines and US 10-year yields drive gold in the meantime.
numbers: CFTC: funds strongly for gold, trimmed

scenarios.base: If yields hold above 5%, gold drifts lower within its range.
scenarios.bull: A big Gulf escalation or a sharp drop in yields brings buyers back.
scenarios.bear: If yields climb further on oil-led inflation fears, gold extends its losing run.
